briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 20, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of the Climate Crisis and International Warnings
sections.content: The damage caused by climate change is intensifying globally, with even Nepal, a low greenhouse gas emitter, experiencing severe impacts, highlighting issues of climate justice [2]. Domestically, the Haenggu Reservoir in front of the Wonju Climate Change Promotion Center is covered in green algae [5], and the frequency of complex disasters is increasing [7], with climate change phenomena such as heatwaves and torrential rains altering students' daily lives [6]. In this context, some companies that fail to adequately respond to the climate crisis are even facing climate lawsuits on charges of breach of trust [8], further increasing corporate responsibility. Internationally, global warming and the El Niño phenomenon have driven atmospheric water vapor levels to an all-time high [61], and large-scale protests against inaction on climate change have taken place in Geneva and Lausanne, Switzerland [59], leading to ongoing global warnings about the climate crisis and commentary on the role of international politics [62].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges Amidst Greenhouse Gas Reduction Efforts
sections.content: Last year, South Korea's total greenhouse gas emissions decreased by 0.9%, showing a continuous downward trend since 2022 [10, 54, 55]. However, net emissions paradoxically increased due to the impact of forest fires [9]. Particularly in the power sector, despite an increase in renewable energy generation, coal power also rose, leading to a 0.2% increase in overall power sector greenhouse gas emissions [48]. This raises concerns that it could impede the achievement of carbon neutrality goals [19, 57]. With greenhouse gas reduction progressing slowly, the surging demand for artificial intelligence (AI) power has led to coal-fired power being reconsidered as a 'security power source' [51], posing a significant challenge. Furthermore, fundamental questions are being raised about whether carbon neutrality is sufficiently addressed by merely being labeled 'eco-friendly' [20]. Amidst these complex disaster situations, there is a growing call for integrated management in a society where one disaster often leads to another [56].

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts to Expand Carbon Neutrality Practices Domestically
sections.content: Active movements to practice carbon neutrality are being observed across the nation. In Uiwang City, the 'Carbon Neutrality Practice Two-Feet Day' event, involving approximately 200 citizens, was successfully held [12, 15, 28, 29, 32, 34], continuing activities that encourage voluntary citizen participation. In Gwangmyeong City, the '2026 Climate Academy' journey, with the participation of youth climate volunteers, was successfully completed [25, 36]. The Cheonan Carbon Neutrality Support Center is actively working to raise awareness by directly visiting citizens and operating 'Let's Practice Carbon Neutrality Together' classes [16]. In the political sphere, Representative Song Ki-heon demonstrated practical commitment by completing a 'Carbon Neutrality Riding' journey, cycling 152km from the National Assembly to Wonju [14, 30]. Furthermore, various entities are striving to spread a carbon-neutral culture: Western Power is discovering carbon neutrality ideas through competitions and linking them to educational programs [11, 22], and Lotte Chilsung is accelerating ESG management across its entire value chain with the goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2040 [33].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Grid Innovation
sections.content: The government has announced ambitious plans to expand renewable energy to 100GW, three times the current level, by 2030 and accelerate the transition to an electric nation, thereby speeding up the securing of alternative energy sources to combat the climate crisis [37, 47]. To achieve these goals, the Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) will be reformed for the first time in 15 years, operating through competitive bidding and long-term contracts starting next year [40]. LS Electric and KEPCO are jointly developing 'grid-forming' technology for distribution to stabilize the renewable energy power grid [44]. Local governments are also actively participating: Pohang City plans to install solar power generation facilities in 30 public parking lots to supply a total of 10MW of renewable energy and contribute to achieving RE100 [38, 39, 41, 46, 52, 53]. Gunpo City has made the nation's first attempt to install solar power generation facilities in soundproof tunnels [31]. Furthermore, proposals are emerging, such as one from the Jangheung County Council suggesting that renewable energy profits should be utilized for residents' income and the region's future financial resources [42], exploring ways in which renewable energy expansion can also contribute to local economic revitalization.

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we examined various domestic and international response efforts amidst the intensifying climate crisis, along with the challenges on the path to carbon neutrality. Continued attention and action will determine the future for all of us. This concludes today's climate briefing.

articles.description: Net emissions increased due to Gyeongbuk wildfires. Last year, domestic total greenhouse gas emissions only decreased by 0.9% compared to the previous year. Large wildfires in Gyeongbuk significantly reduced forest areas, leading to an increase in net emissions.
